Cosmic: Relating to the universe and the natural processes that happen in it.
Costly: Expensive, especially in a way that is surprising or not convenient.
Costume: The set of clothes typical of a particular country or period of history, or suitable for a particular activity.
Cottage: A small house, usually in the countryside.
Cotton: The soft white substance that grows around the seeds of a tall plant from warm countries, or the cloth made from it.
Cough: To force air out of your lungs with a sudden loud noise.
Counsel: To give advice, especially on social or personal problems.
Count: To say numbers one after the other in order, or to calculate the number of people or things in a group.
Counterpart: A person or thing that has the same purpose as another one in a different place or organization.
Countless: Very many, or too many to be counted.
Country: An area of land that has its own government, army, etc.
Countryside: Land which is away from towns and cities.
Courtesy: Polite behavior, or a polite action or remark.
Cow: A large female animal kept for its milk or meat.
Cowboy: A man, especially in the western US, whose job is to take care of cattle, and who often rides a horse.
Crawl: To move along on hands and knees or with your body stretched out along a surface.
Crazy: Stupid or not reasonable, or mentally ill.
Cream: The thick pale yellow or white fatty liquid that rises to the top of milk.
Creation: The act of creating something, or the thing that is created.
Creative: Producing or using original and unusual ideas.
Creativity: The ability to produce original and unusual ideas, or to make something new or imaginative.
Cricket: A sport played by two teams of eleven players, using a bat and ball on a field with two sets of three sticks called wickets.
Criminal: A person who has committed a crime.
Critic: Someone whose job is to give their opinion about something, especially movies, books, music, etc.
Criticism: An opinion given about something or someone, especially a negative opinion, or the activity of making such judgments.
Crown: A circular decoration for the head, usually made of gold and jewels and worn by a king or queen.
Cruise: A journey on a large ship for pleasure, during which you visit several places.
Cube: A solid object with six square sides of equal size.
Cucumber: A long, thin, pale green vegetable with watery flesh and a dark green skin, which is usually eaten raw in salads.
Cue: A signal for someone to do something.
Cultural: Relating to the habits, traditions, and beliefs of a society.
Cup: A small, round container, often with a handle, used for drinking tea, coffee, etc.
Curb: To control or limit something that is not wanted.
Curiosity: An eager wish to know or learn about something.
Curl: A piece of hair which grows or has been made into a curve.
Currency: The money that is used in a particular country at a particular time.
Curriculum: The group of subjects studied in a school, college, etc.
Curtain: A piece of material, especially cloth, that hangs across a window or opening to make a room or part of a room dark or private.
Cut: To break the surface of something, or to divide or make something smaller, using a sharp tool, especially a knife.
Cute: Attractive in a pretty or endearing way.
Dam: A wall built across a river that stops the water and can also be used to produce electricity.
Damn: A word used to express anger.
Dance: To move the body and feet to music.
Dangerous: A person, animal, thing, or activity that could harm you.
Darkness: The state of being dark, without any light.
Darling: A person who is very much loved or liked.
Database: A large amount of information storedNormally I can help with things like this, but I don't seem to have access to that content. You can try again or ask me for something else.
Accustomed: Familiar with something so that it seems normal or usual.
Adhere: To stick firmly to a surface or to follow a set of rules.
Affluent: Having a lot of money or owning many expensive things.
Aggravate: To make a bad situation or an illness even worse.
Annihilate: To destroy something completely so that nothing is left.
Apprehensive: Feeling worried or nervous about something that you are going to do.
Arduous: Difficult, needing a lot of effort and energy over a long period.
Atheist: A person who does not believe in any gods.
Atrocious: Of very bad quality; extremely unpleasant or cruel.
Augment: To increase the size or value of something by adding to it.
Avert: To prevent something bad from happening; to turn away.
Boisterous: Someone who is noisy, energetic, and rough in a happy way.
Breezy: Happy, confident, and relaxed; also describes a place with light wind.
Brittle: Delicate and easily broken into many pieces.
Capricious: Changing mood or behavior suddenly and unexpectedly.
Complacent: Feeling too satisfied with yourself so that you stop trying to improve.
Empathy: The ability to share someone else's feelings or experiences.
Enigma: Something that is mysterious and impossible to understand.
Equivocal: Not clear and seeming to have two possible meanings.
Erratic: Not regular or certain; moving in an unpredictable way.
Escalate: To become or make something become greater or more serious.
Fickle: Likely to change your opinion or your feelings suddenly.
Flamboyant: Very confident in behavior, or intended to be noticed.
Futile: Having no effect or achieving nothing; pointless.
Grievance: A complaint or a strong feeling that you have been treated unfairly.
Haphazard: Not having an obvious order or plan; lacking organization.
Minimize: To reduce something to the least possible amount or degree.
Negligent: Not being careful enough or failing to take care of something.
Notorious: Famous for something bad or immoral.
Nurture: To help a plan or person to develop and be successful.
Obscure: Not known to many people; difficult to understand.
Obsolete: No longer used because something newer and better exists.
Obstinate: Unwilling to change your opinion or your behavior.
Ominous: Suggesting that something unpleasant is going to happen.
Optimistic: Hoping or believing that good things will happen in the future.
Paradox: A situation or statement that seems impossible because it has two opposite factors.
Peculiar: Unusual and strange, sometimes in an unpleasant way.
Perpetual: Continuing forever in the same way.
Persist: To continue to do something despite difficulties or opposition.
Pessimistic: Thinking that bad things are more likely to happen than good things.
Plausible: Seeming likely to be true, or able to be believed.
Pragmatic: Solving problems in a sensible way that suits the conditions.
Precarious: In a dangerous state because of not being safe or firmly fixed.
Prevalent: Existing very commonly or happening often.
Procrastinate: To keep delaying something that must be done.
Quaint: Attractive because of being unusual and old-fashioned.
Relentless: Continuing in a severe or determined way without stopping.
Reluctant: Not willing to do something and therefore slow to do it.
Resilient: Able to be happy or successful again after something difficult.
Reticent: Unwilling to speak about your thoughts or feelings.
Sarcastic: Using remarks that clearly mean the opposite of what you say to hurt feelings.
Scrutinize: To examine something very carefully in order to discover information.
Serene: Peaceful and calm; worried by nothing.
Spontaneous: Happening or done in a natural, often sudden way, without any planning.
Subtle: Not loud, bright, noticeable, or obvious in any way.
Superfluous: More than is needed or wanted.
Tedious: Boring and tiring because of being too long or slow.
Tentative: Not certain or agreed, or done without confidence.
Ubiquitous: Seeming to be everywhere at the same time.
Unanimous: In complete agreement; everyone having the same opinion.
Vague: Not clearly expressed, known, described, or decided.
Versatile: Able to change easily from one activity to another.
Vibrant: Energetic, exciting, and full of enthusiasm.
Vindictive: Having or showing a strong desire for revenge.
Vivid: Descriptions or memories which produce very clear images in the mind.
Wary: Not completely trusting or certain about something or someone.
Whimsical: Unusual and strange in a way that might be funny or annoying.
Zenith: The best or most successful point or time.
